verdict.rationale: LibreChat's source is hosted in a public GitHub repository (github.com/danny-avila/LibreChat), and community users describe it as open source under the MIT license. Skepticism about a possible future license change after the acquisition is speculation, not a contradiction, so it does not dispute the current open license. Missing for 10: a first-party statement of the license (e.g., a LICENSE file or docs page) in the evidence, and explicit first-party documentation of source availability rather than inference from the repo URL.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: LibreChat was my favorite open source frontend/backend for interacting with LLMs.
